|---|---|---|---|---|

## 2. CONFIRMED: the two predicates still disagree, so the invariant claim at `DEFERRED-FIXES.md:486-488` is false as written

The doc says `engine.js:1315` and the split's skip clause at `:346` "finally agree". They do not. `app/js/store.js:345` is guarded by `!e.id`:

```js
if (!e.id && !stackable && !(e.qty > 0) && !(e.qty != null && e.qty <= 0)) e.qty = 1;
```

A row that **already carries an `id` but no `qty`** is skipped, and so is every stackable row. - Inventory → Stash renders **"Stash / 0 ENTRIES / Empty. The Undercut is open"**.
- `encumbrance.current` **0**, item list empty.

| `qty` | id-less non-stackable | id-carrying | stackable |
|---|---|---|---|
| absent / `null` / `NaN` / `"abc"` / `{}` | normalized to 1, id minted, agrees | **q unchanged, vis=false own=true — DISAGREE** | **DISAGREE** |
| `0` / `-2` / `""` / `"0"` / `[]` / `false` | untouched, both say unowned | agrees | agrees |
| `"3"` | splits into 3 × qty 1 | stays one row `"3"` | pooled |
| `1.5` / `" 2 "` / `"2.7"` | 2 / 2 / 3 instances | unchanged | pooled |

The `!e.id` guard buys nothing: dropping it would set `qty=1` and the very next line (`if (e.id || …)`) still pushes the row unsplit. `engine.loadCatalogItem` (`app/js/engine.js:934-945`) searches exactly seven pools — `melee/ranged/signature.items/signature.munitions/ammo/armor/tools`. It does **not** search `partItems()`, `armorModItems()`, `vehicleItems()`, `vehicleModItems()`, all of which `inventory.findItem` (`app/js/inventory.js:232-248`) does include. So `isStackableItem(null) === true` (`engine.js:862`) classes every bench Part, armor Mod, vehicle and vehicle mod as **stackable**, and fix 2 never touches them.

## Finding 1: the collision class is not gone, only one of its two doors

`app/js/store.js:346` -- `if (e.id || !(e.qty > 0) || stackable) { splitEquipment.push(e); return; }`

The split is the one place that could enforce entry identity, and it skips any row that already carries an `id` without ever checking that the id is unique. A **duplicate** `e.id` reproduces the L9 defect set verbatim.

Scenario, measured: import a record with
`equipment: [{id:"eq_DUP", name:"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]", qty:1}, {id:"eq_DUP", name:"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]", qty:1}]`

- `EN.engine.ownedRigs` returns two entries with one distinct key (`["eq_DUP","eq_DUP"]`).
- 23 damage on the picked rig: **both rows read 17/40**. One shared damage slot.
- The picker renders `key:eq_DUP :: Black Clinic [5] #1` and `key:eq_DUP :: Black Clinic [5] #2`, two options with the identical value, so #2 is unaddressable.
- The Fabrication bench prints `Advanced Medkit (Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]) · PROFICIENT` **twice** and Medtech reads **Edge 7** against the correct **Edge 6** for the same character with unique ids. The Advanced Medkit's Edge Die is granted twice.

Those are the four defects `DEFERRED-FIXES.md` L9 records as closed, at the same severity, with the same reachability class: not producible in-app (every insertion path mints a fresh id, `inventory.js:106` and `builder.js:993`, and the report is right about that), reachable by import and hand-edit. It is also the *most likely* hand-edit: duplicating an equipment row in an exported JSON is how a player adds a second rig, and copy-paste carries the id.

The consequence for step 5 is the load-bearing part. The invariant the fix comment states at `store.js:336-339`, and which `DEFERRED-FIXES.md:364-365`, `:485-488` and `:808` restate as the floor `ch.armorDR` and `ch.shieldWear` will stand on, is "every owned non-stackable row carries an `eq_` id". That is true, and it is not the invariant a per-piece map needs. It needs one *unique* id per owned row. Two duplicate-id armor pieces will share one DR and one wear slot exactly as these two rigs share one damage slot, and step 5 will have keyed on `entryKey` believing the floor was solid. Either the split should mint a fresh id for a duplicate (a seen-ids set in the same `forEach`, a few lines beside the `qty` normalization), or the invariant should be written down as the weaker thing it actually is so step 5 does not lean on it.
